item.text: {"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Generally separated: the USMCA filing is explicitly treated as an allegation rather than a breach finding, and ASF pending-clarification amounts and procurement-risk flags are not called proven loss, bribery, or misconduct. Residual risk remains where administration-level responsibility for flagship projects, health-program design, and energy orientation could be overstated as AMLO’s personal direction.","closed_system_silence":"Material risk. Federal procurement, Pemex, health, and project implementation are partly closed administrative systems; incomplete/late procurement records and unavailable final audit-action status could conceal misconduct or correction.","duplicate_reporting":"Several records are same-family or superseding duplicates and should not be treated as independent corroboration: WEB-5B-005/034, 009/035, 010/028, and 015/020. OECD, IMF, CONEVAL, ASF, and official administrative records also repeatedly describe overlapping underlying outcomes.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Yes. The notebook documents favorable evidence on fiscal restraint, wage policy, transfers, employment, poverty reduction, FDI, and corrective energy work, alongside adverse evidence on targeting, health access/design, procurement risk, buffers, energy rules, and project audits.","missing_source_type":"Independent causal evaluations and final audit-action/resolution records are missing: especially minimum-wage and transfer effects by group, completed ASF recovery/liability status, project economics, and event-level evidence of executive correction or finance-minister autonomy.","official_claim_independence":"Official legal, administrative, and response records are usually paired with independent or statutory sources where the claim is interpretive. Remaining gaps concern government FDI, wage-policy intent, energy-response effectiveness, and Pemex response claims, which lack equally direct independent verification.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Moderate risk. Trade complaints, media reporting, and procurement-risk reporting can make visible disputes appear more prevalent or severe than adjudicated facts warrant; the notebook appropriately retains allegation and methodology caveats.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Substantially addressed. The record distinguishes informal and extremely poor households, gender and regional gaps, executive versus tripartite/autonomous authority, inherited fiscal and institutional conditions, reopening, U.S. demand, remittances, commodity shocks, and inflation. Causal incidence remains incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-5B-001","WEB-5B-002","WEB-5B-003","WEB-5B-006","WEB-5B-007","WEB-5B-011","WEB-5B-021","WEB-5B-023","WEB-5B-025","WEB-5B-026","WEB-5B-028","WEB-5B-029","WEB-5B-030","WEB-5B-031","WEB-5B-032","WEB-5B-033","WEB-5B-034","WEB-5B-035"],"unresolved_risks":["No event-level evidence establishes Ramírez de la O’s autonomy in contested 2022 decisions.","ASF observations and pending-clarification amounts lack reliable final action-level resolution.","No causal evaluation isolates minimum-wage, transfer, reopening, remittance, and labor-demand effects on household outcomes.","Energy consultation and official work-plan evidence do not establish a treaty breach or successful correction.","Project-quality and FDI figures do not establish net investment quality, additionality, or long-run productivity effects."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":31,"independent_source_family_estimate":13,"missing_themes":["5B.1/5B.8: causal distributional effects of the 2022 minimum-wage increase and transfers, particularly among informal and extremely poor households.","5B.2: direct evidence of professional autonomy or constrained delegation for the finance minister in an actual contested 2022 decision.","5B.4/5B.6: independent evidence on investment quality, sectoral deterrence, flagship-project economics, and productivity effects rather than aggregate FDI or recommendations alone.","5B.5/5B.6/5B.7: final ASF action, recovery, liability, and remediation status for the cited procurement, health, and Tren Maya audit matters.","5B.7: dated evidence that executive decision-makers acted on or declined specific warnings concerning procurement, health access, Pemex, targeting, or project appraisal."],"substantive_issues":["The ledger retains superseded or same-family duplicate copies; these must not inflate independence or evidence counts.","WEB-5B-030 bundles materially distinct audit results across multiple Tren Maya segments in one source-claim unit; audit-level facts need separable treatment downstream.","WEB-5B-031 combines multiple state and INSABI audit findings; this is not a claim that the dossier is complete.","The chapter has a broad, balanced set of target-period evidence with explicit attribution, contrary-evidence, and temporal caveats, sufficient for downstream interpretation only with material confidence limits.","Residual gaps are preserved for confidence and interpretation downstream; no further continuation is permitted in this terminal review."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"For the selected 5B lenses, the dossier contains numerous identifiable, mostly precise, target-period source-claim units across independent institutional families and handles principal favorable/adverse evidence fairly.
